newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-O'MEARA LEADS WESTERN OPEN BY STROKE AFTER FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-O'MEARA LEADS WESTERN OPEN BY STROKE AFTER FIRST ROUND.

text.p: Mark O'Meara narrowly upstaged friend and neighbour Tiger Woods to take the first-round lead at the $2 million Motorola Western Open Thursday.
O'Meara made a fine birdie at his final hole to shoot six-under-par 66 in a testing wind on the highly rated Cog Hill course on the outskirts of Chicago.
He enjoyed a one-stroke advantage over fellow Americans Woods, Phil Blackmar, Jim Furyk and Dave Stockton Jr.
Playing in a threesome which included Woods, the 40-year-old O'Meara was overpowered but not overawed.
"My short game was good today, and that pretty much carried me through the round," said O'Meara, who has won twice on the PGA Tour this year.

"I've played a lot of golf with Tiger. I use him as a motivating factor. Look at how hard the kid goes at the ball and keeps his balance and still hits it pretty darn straight. He goes at it unbelieveably hard, yet he's got great control.

"If I tried to swing that hard, I would be all over the place. He has a huge advantage on me. I have nothing but admiration for somebody who can come out at an early age and dominate the game the way he has already done.
"But I feel that if I putt well and drive the ball in the fairway, I can play as well as any other player out here on tour."
O'Meara revealed his class at his final hole, the par-five ninth, where he hit a bunker shot from 72 yards and sank a 14-footer to take the outright lead.
Woods, refreshed after a week off, accrued seven birdies and two bogeys in an ominous return to form just two weeks before the British Open.
He putted poorly to finish equal 19th at the U.S. Open three weeks ago, then struggled to a tie for 43rd at the Buick Classic at Westchester the following week.
However, a week off was just what the doctor ordered, and Woods obviously welcomed the rest at his home in an exclusive Orlando gated community.
"I was tired. When I went home last week I put the clubs away for a bit," explained the Masters champion. "I fished with Mark (O'Meara) but mostly I was a couch potato."
Woods also enjoyed playing here with O'Meara: "Mark has been a big brother on tour. He's taken me under his wing and shown me the ropes."

Six of Woods' birdies came from inside five feet, but he said he did not hit his approach shots as well as it looked. "Some of the shots weren't that good but I got away with them. The wind was my friend. Some of my misses turned out pretty well."
